steps.text: Place turkey drumsticks and water in a large soup pot and bring to a boil. Stir in onions, carrots, celery, garlic, salt, black pepper, sage, thyme, rosemary, and celery salt; reduce heat to a simmer. Cook until turkey meat is very tender, about 2 hours.
Remove drumsticks and allow to cool enough to handle. Remove meat from bones and tendons, chop meat, and return to soup. Discard bones.
Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Cook egg noodles in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain.
Divide noodles among soup bowls and ladle turkey soup on top.

raw_recipe.headline: Old Man's Turkey Noodle Soup
raw_recipe.description: This old-fashioned turkey noodle soup is hearty and simple to make with leftover turkey in a savory broth for a flavorsome post-holiday meal.

review.reviewBody: been doing this for ages only I use the turkey carcass after Thenksgiving. Great way to use all the bird.

Had some leftover turkey and wanted to make a good soup. This was it!!! Only changes I made was to use chicken broth instead of water and omitted the 1 Tbsp salt since I wouldn't be cooking the turkey in the water. I mixed everything together, put it in the Crock Pot on High for an hour to cook the vegetables then turned to Low for about 4 hrs. Add the cooked noodles to the pot about 10 minutes before serving to give them more flavor. I served these with hot biscuits and got rave reviews from my family! Just right for a cold rainy night! Thanks for posting!

This is a very flavorful soup! The small amount of spices are perfect for the quantity of broth and don't overwhelm but enhance the recipe. It makes you wonder, "Wow, this is great, what are those delicious flavors?" I modified it by sauteing garlic, onion, spices (only used 1/4 tsp sage but given amounts of all other spices) and celery in 1/2 stick melted butter. Then I whisked 1/2 cup flour into 1 cup milk--ended up having to add chicken broth to thin--and poured into sauteed mix. To this I added 6 cups chicken broth, 4 or 5 cups water and 1 tsp Better than Bouillon chicken flavor. I used fresh celery leaves. I also added 1/2 cup canned corn, 1 tblspn Hormel real bacon bits (these turned out to be undetectable and one should either add more or omit), and pre-cooked, 2.5 or 3 cups shredded turkey breast instead of dark meat and 4 cups egg noodles. It's absolutely delicious, mild yet flavorful and a fantastic way to use left-over holiday turkey. I will definitely be adding this to my repertoire!

I made this tonight. I had already made bone broth (which is a richer broth) with my turkey carcass, so it was just a matter of adding the vegetables, your spices, and the turkey pieces to it. I decided to saute the vegetables and the spices in olive oil before adding to the already-made bone broth. Your combination of spices is fantastic! Thanks for sharing! I'll be saving this recipe for future use!

Let me just say that this is one of the best soup recipes ever! I have made this several times and am just now writing this review. You can make this as is and it will be delicious. Since I am not one to waste anything, I used this recipe along with my Thanksgiving turkey carcass. I put the carcass and the drumsticks in an 8 quart stock pot, covered the contents with water and started the creation process. I pretty much doubled the spices and added additional veggies, but the outcome was fantastic. Since there are Keto dietary requirements in this household, I also cooked some collard greens using just broth from this soup and substituted the collard greens for the egg noodles. That was also a big hit. I am also a dad and I cook everything! Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

I made this from left over turkey bones. My tip is to place all the turkey bones from cutting up a turkey and placing them on tin foil and bake the bones until they are nice and brown and crispy looking. Then I boil them in the water from potatoes and the broth has so much more flavour. 
I followed the rest of this recipe and if was yummy.
Deb

This recipes is a keeper. So simple. I have made this twice. Once as written and then tonight I only had 2 legs and a thigh..which was plenty. Before serving I added lemon juice and some dill..delicious!

I love this soup! I boiled the leftover carcass of my Christmas turkey for several hours, removed the solids by using a strainer and had the 3 quarts of broth. In my stock pot, I sautéed the onion, celery and carrot, along with the spices and herbs in a small amount of olive oil until softened. Then added back in the broth and several cups of cut up white and dark meat. I brought to a boil then reduced heat and allowed it to simmer for about an hour before adding in the cooked noodles. Delicious and So easy!

Fabulous!!!!! I was looking for a soup to use the leftover turkey from the bone in turkey breasts I had made earlier in the week. I followed the basic recipe but made a few adjustments. I had 4 cups turkey breast meat and also the carcass from the turkey breast and used that instead of the drumsticks. I used 9 cups water and 3 cans low sodium chicken broth. The seasoning was perfect but I doubled the sage, thyme and rosemary since I was making a larger batch. I added the 4 cups turkey at the end. I also threw in a cup each of frozen peas and corn at the end and used Ronzoni whole grain egg noodles that I added right to the pot (a 12 oz package). The house smells amazing and the soup tastes even better. Perfect combination of flavors! This ones a keeper!

I wanted to make a turkey noodle soup with our turkey left overs and I used this recipe as my starter. Since I was using cooked turkey instead of drumsticks, I let the other recipes ingredients simmer in 8 cups of chicken broth for 30 minutes before I added the turkey meat. Once I added the turkey, I let that simmer for 40 minutes and added a bag of the frozen "homemade" noodles and happened to glance at their recipe for "chicken noodle soup" and theirs called for adding 1/2 cup flour with a cup of milk mixed together in a leak proof jar and poured into the broth as a thickener and to add 3 more cups of milk to the soup once the noodles had cooked for 30 minutes. It was oh so very yummy!! Saved this one in my recipe box!

We loved this soup, but I did make some changes. I used my turkey drippings and leftover gravy along with chicken broth in place of the water. I was out of sage, so I used 1 tsp. of poultry seasoning in place of the individual seasonings. I didn't add any salt, because I didn't use water and with the addition of the fresh celery, I did see the need for the celery salt. I have also found that soups with pasta, when leftovers are stored, the pasta absorbs all of the broth. I add my noodles as I serve the soup. You can precook noodles and store them with a little melted butter to keep them from sticking to each other. We liked the soup better than the turkey dinner.

This was a good soup, comforting and satisfying. I wasn't sure if the drumsticks were supposed to be raw or already roasted. I used a leftover drumstick from Thanksgiving. It worked very well. I used chicken broth instead of water. This was a good low-fiber soup.
tasty and satisfying! Could swap the noodles for rice or potatoes possibly.

I really liked it .Used chicken thighs instead of turkey...it's what I had. I will shorten up the noodles next time cause I don't like them slopping against my chin with every spoonful. Will also use turkey.
The best recipe i've tried so far
It was so good followed to a T we loved it and it will be added to our recipe book.
Why wouldn't you just cook the noodles in the turkey broth why cook it in plain water that enhances the flavor into the noodles and thickens the broth. Everything else is pretty basic.

I was missing thyme so used poultry seasoning - probably not as good but still delicious. I also used Costco egg noodles which are not flat so 2 cups of noodles did not work - just poured in a bunch. The problem with leftovers is the noodles absorb all of the wonderful broth - next time I will separate the broth before putting it in the fridge.
